name: Blend Labs, Inc.

profile.description: Blend Labs provides cloud-based origination software that powers the digital interface between banks, credit unions and mortgage lenders and their consumers, covering mortgages, home equity, personal loans, credit cards and deposit accounts. Its Autopilot agentic-AI orchestration layer automates lending workflows. Founded in 2012 by CEO Nima Ghamsari, a former Palantir employee, and headquartered in San Francisco, Blend reported Q2 2026 revenue of $33.8M (+7%), including $31.4M of software platform revenue, with non-GAAP operating income above guidance. Q3 2026 guidance of $31.5-33.5M implies roughly flat year-on-year revenue amid higher mortgage rates. Market cap is about $265M at $1.12 per share.

innovation.label: STRONG
innovation.analysis: Track Record (2/3): Blend refocused on pure software, exiting its title business, which FY2025 reports as discontinued operations, and launched Autopilot in 2026 as an agentic orchestration layer for lending workflows [1][6]. Q1 2026 revenue grew 15% to $30.8M with non-GAAP operating income of $4.1M [3]. AI Deployment (2/2): Autopilot is a shipping AI product. As of May 2026, 65 lenders had activated it, 22 were running it live and it had processed more than 7,000 applications, with paid pricing from the end of June 2026; Ghamsari also reports more than 1.5x engineering productivity from internal AI adoption [3]. Market Share (1/2): Blend is a meaningful digital-origination player with top-20 bank wins, but ICE Mortgage Technology's Encompass has a far larger installed base [3]. Pipeline (1/2): Management says Autopilot and internal agents could add 10-15% incremental top-line growth in 2027, though the Q3 2026 revenue guide of $31.5-33.5M shows near-term softness [2][3]. R&D Intensity (1/1): FY2025 R&D was $32.8M, 26.6% of $123.6M revenue, which is top-quartile for fintech software [6].

inspiration.label: DEVELOPING
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (3/4): Blend exists to make obtaining financial products simple and transparent. Ghamsari founded it after seeing mortgage inefficiency firsthand and frames the work as removing roughly $11,000 of human cost per mortgage, a specific purpose that has guided 14 years of strategy, including the title exit and the Autopilot pivot [4]. Community Impact (0/2): No distinctive charitable or community programs were found for the roughly 400-person company [5]. Employee Retention (1/2): The founder-CEO has led for 14 years and Ghamsari publicly described a post-IPO reset to get 'really, really great at one thing' after multiple layoff rounds. Leadership continuity is a positive, but no turnover data was found, so this is average [4]. Insider Buying (0/2): No meaningful open-market insider buying was found. Prior company buybacks are corporate actions, not executive conviction [3].

infrastructure.label: DEVELOPING
infrastructure.analysis: Calculated mechanically with Growth weights (ROE 2x, 5yr revenue CAGR 2x, Forward PEG 2x). Metric scores: D/E 2.2% (1.0), effectively debt-free [7]; ROE 2.1% (0.14, 2x) [7]; revenue growth YoY 7.0% (0.90), Q2 2026 [1]; 5yr revenue CAGR ~5.2% (0.68, 2x), derived from FMP revenue of $96.0M in FY2020 (before the title acquisition) and $123.6M in FY2025 (title reported as discontinued) [6]; Forward P/E 18.7 (1.0) [7]; profit margin 0.02% (0.0), essentially breakeven on a GAAP basis [7]; FMP forward PEG -0.05, negative and therefore 0.0 (2x), despite positive non-GAAP operating income [6]. Weighted sum is 4.54 out of 10, which rounds to 5. Liquidity passes at about $2.3M of daily traded value ($1.12 x 2.03M shares), but at roughly 2x the $1M floor it is thin for institutional trading.

ai_resilience.label: MODERATE
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (6/9): Blend's origination platform is embedded in regulated lender workflows (TRID, HMDA, ECOA compliance) with deep loan-origination-system integrations that create real switching costs, so a generic AI tool cannot simply replace it [1][6]. The exposure is real, however: AI document-processing and decisioning tools from ICE and AI-native startups could commoditize parts of the workflow, and Blend's scale (about $124M revenue) limits how much it can invest defensively. AI Opportunity (1/1): Blend is monetizing AI directly. Autopilot moved to paid pricing in mid-2026 after 65 lender activations and 7,000+ applications processed, and management targets 10-15% incremental 2027 growth from AI agents [3].

infinite_game.summary: Through Sinek's lens, Blend shows real infinite traits under founder Nima Ghamsari. Fourteen years pursuing simpler, cheaper consumer lending, the willingness to exit the title business and give up revenue for focus, and an early bet on agentic AI all point to purpose-led choices. Ghamsari's candour about post-IPO overreach fits the self-awareness Sinek values. But repeated layoffs, a share price down more than 90% from the IPO and a narrative about winning lender deals keep it MIXED.

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (2/3): The cause of removing friction and cost (about $11,000 of human cost per mortgage) from consumer lending has been consistent since 2012 and visibly drives decisions such as the title exit and Autopilot [4]. It has not yet been validated over decades or through leadership transitions.

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (1/2): Founder continuity and a deliberate flat-title culture support trust, and internal AI adoption has lifted engineering output more than 1.5x [3][4]. Multiple post-IPO layoff rounds dented the Circle of Safety, and no turnover data was found.

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (0/1): Communications focus on Blend's own wins, Autopilot adoption and deal pipeline, with no evidence of acknowledging what ICE Mortgage Technology or other rivals do better [1][3].

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (1/2): Blend moved from mortgage-only software to a broader consumer-banking suite, exited title and is now re-architecting around agentic AI with Autopilot [3][6]. These are meaningful pivots within lending software rather than a full reinvention.

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (1/2): Exiting title to refocus on software and rebuilding the product around Autopilot were costly, long-term choices, as was Ghamsari publicly admitting the company 'had taken on too many things' [4][6]. At Blend's small scale, these bets are as much about survival as sacrifice.

investment_thesis: Blend has a debt-free balance sheet (D/E 2.2%), 75% gross margins and positive non-GAAP operating income, and it is one of the first mortgage-software vendors to put agentic AI into production [1][7]. Autopilot reached 65 activated lenders and more than 7,000 applications before paid pricing began in mid-2026, and management sees AI agents adding 10-15% incremental growth in 2027 [3]. At about $265M market cap, roughly 2x sales and 18.7x forward earnings, a mortgage-rate decline that revives origination volumes, combined with Autopilot monetization, could drive meaningful upside [7].
thesis_continued: The bear case: growth is stalling, with Q2 2026 revenue up 7% and Q3 guidance of $31.5-33.5M implying roughly flat year-on-year revenue, below consensus, and the stock fell about 10% on that outlook [1][2]. GAAP profitability is barely breakeven (0.02% margin, 2.1% ROE), the forward PEG is negative, and revenue is highly sensitive to mortgage rates and refinance volumes [6][7]. Competition from ICE Mortgage Technology, which has a far larger installed base, and AI-native entrants could compress pricing, and at $1.12 with about $2.3M of daily traded value, liquidity is thin. The Inspire Impact Score of +35 (ALIGNED) is a modest positive for faith-based investors.
key_catalysts: Autopilot paid conversion: moving the 65 activated lenders to paid contracts could add the 10-15% incremental 2027 growth management has outlined [3]
Mortgage-rate relief driving a refinance and purchase-origination rebound that lifts Blend's volume-based software revenue [2][3]
Q3 2026 results and 2027 outlook showing renewed growth from top-20 bank wins and Consumer Banking Suite expansion [1][2]
key_risks: Revenue stagnation: Q3 2026 guidance of $31.5-33.5M implies roughly flat year-on-year revenue and missed consensus, reflecting mortgage-rate headwinds and customer volume roll-off [2]
Competitive and AI commoditization pressure from ICE Mortgage Technology (Encompass) and AI-native document and decisioning startups on a roughly $124M revenue base [6]
Thin profitability and liquidity: a GAAP margin near 0%, a negative forward PEG and about $2.3M of daily traded value at $1.12 per share heighten volatility and capital-raising risk [7]
